card.name: Subject right before could/would/should
card.fires_on: A subject word (it, they, he, or a noun) in narrative history text, just before a modal verb like could, would or should. The modal is usually in a conditional or reported clause.

modes.label: Pronoun before modal
modes.description: A pronoun subject in an if, as or that clause is followed by could, would or should.
modes.example: he again exhorted the door to speak, saying that, if it feared to utter the name aloud,<< it>> could whisper in his ear.

modes.label: Noun subject before modal
modes.description: A noun or title ends the subject and a modal verb comes next.
modes.example: Head<<rights>>, it was provided by law, could

card.writes: It promotes 'might' and suppresses 'may', which favors past-style modals over 'may'.
card.plain: It fires on the subject of a sentence just before a verb like could or would in old-style historical prose.
